⚠️ Closed alpha — provisional docs. The opendefense-platform is under breaking development; verify against the code before relying on details.

This is the core integrator recipe: making your data appear on every enrolled TAK client automatically — from a script or service, no UI, no ATAK plugin. It comes down to three curl calls against the Marti REST API on :8443 with a client certificate you already have in the cluster. Two companion pages cover what this one takes as given: What you can show in TAK clients for choosing the right data shape, and Defining standard data sources for content that should ship with every client instead. Worked example: drone weather in ATAK runs this recipe end to end.

Identity: whose certificate publishes?

Marti authenticates by mTLS client certificate, and two identities work — they are not equivalent:

  • The **tak-server-admin** certificate — the cert-manager Certificate tak-server-admin in namespace app-tak, the same credential takrmapi presents when driving TAK from inside the pod (mounted there as /data/persistent/{public,private}/mtlsclient.*). For host-side scripting, pull it straight from the Secret:

kubectl get secret -n app-tak tak-server-admin -o jsonpath='{.data.tls\.crt}' | base64 -d > tls.crt
kubectl get secret -n app-tak tak-server-admin -o jsonpath='{.data.tls\.key}' | base64 -d > tls.key
curl -sk --cert tls.crt --key tls.key https://tak.<domain>:8443/Marti/api/missions

• An enrolled user's PEM — any client certificate issued through RASENMAEHER enrollment (a .pfx, password = callsign, converted to PEM) also works against Marti. A firstuser-created admin actually holds more privilege than the platform credential: it gets 200 on /Marti/api/inputs where the tak-server-admin cert now gets 403. If your integration manages inputs, enroll an admin identity and publish with that.

-k is needed against the local deployment — the server cert chains to the internal CA (see TAK stack (Kubernetes)).

The three-call publish flow

blocks.code:
sequenceDiagram
    participant pub as publisher (cron / CI)
    participant marti as Marti API :8443
    participant sync as Enterprise Sync
    participant atak as every ATAK client
    pub->>marti: 1. PUT /Marti/api/missions/dronewx?defaultRole=MISSION_SUBSCRIBER
    Note over pub,marti: 201 created or 409 already exists - both fine
    pub->>marti: 2. POST /Marti/sync/missionupload?hash=sha256 (multipart, field assetfile)
    marti->>sync: store blob, dedupe on hash
    pub->>marti: 3. PUT /Marti/api/missions/dronewx/contents  body {"hashes":[...]}
    sync-->>atak: listed under Available Packages (Tool public)
    marti-->>atak: content change pushed to mission subscribers

blocks.html: A publishing script is short enough to show whole — this is the one used by the worked example, reduced to its essentials:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -Eeuo pipefail

FILE="${1:-dronewx.kmz}"
MISSION="${2:-dronewx}"
HOST="${TAK_HOST:-127.0.0.1}"   # kind hostPort; or tak.<domain> from outside
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

kubectl get secret -n app-tak tak-server-admin -o jsonpath='{.data.tls\.crt}' | base64 -d > "$TMP/tls.crt"
kubectl get secret -n app-tak tak-server-admin -o jsonpath='{.data.tls\.key}' | base64 -d > "$TMP/tls.key"
CURL=(curl -sk --fail-with-body --cert "$TMP/tls.crt" --key "$TMP/tls.key")

HASH="$(shasum -a 256 "$FILE" | cut -d' ' -f1)"

# idempotent: mission create returns 201/409, upload dedupes on hash
"${CURL[@]}" -X PUT -o /dev/null \
  "https://$HOST:8443/Marti/api/missions/$MISSION?creatorUid=dronewx&defaultRole=MISSION_SUBSCRIBER&description=Drone+weather+demo" || true
"${CURL[@]}" -o /dev/null -F "assetfile=@$FILE" \
  "https://$HOST:8443/Marti/sync/missionupload?hash=$HASH&filename=$(basename "$FILE")&creatorUid=dronewx"
"${CURL[@]}" -X PUT -o /dev/null -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"hashes\":[\"$HASH\"]}" \
  "https://$HOST:8443/Marti/api/missions/$MISSION/contents?creatorUid=dronewx"

Three calls, three distinct jobs. The mission PUT creates a named container — defaultRole=MISSION_SUBSCRIBER means anyone joining it gets subscriber rights, so content changes are pushed to them. The missionupload POST puts the blob into Enterprise Sync, keyed by its sha256 — the multipart field name must be assetfile, and the hash goes in the query string. The contents PUT attaches the blob to the mission by hash, body {"hashes":["<sha256>"]} with Content-Type: application/json.

The flow is deliberately idempotent: mission create returns 201 or 409 (both fine), the upload dedupes on hash, and re-attaching an existing hash is harmless — re-running the script with unchanged content is a no-op. To retire an old version:
curl ... -X DELETE "https://$HOST:8443/Marti/api/missions/dronewx/contents?hash=$OLD_HASH&creatorUid=dronewx"

What every client sees

Two visibility channels fire at once:

  • Enterprise Sync is global. Every missionupload is listed by GET /Marti/sync/search with Tool: public — it appears in every client's Data Packages > Available Packages, with or without any mission subscription. Publishing at all already reaches everyone; the mission is what adds push.
  • Mission subscribers get it automatically. Clients subscribed to the mission receive content changes without touching the UI again — republish and it arrives.

A package published this way appears in the client's Available Packages list, and Download files its contents by type: vector KMZs into atak/overlays/, raster KMZs into atak/grg/.

Package before you publish

Upload Mission Package zips, never raw files. A raw KMZ pushed as a server package gets unzipped file-by-file on the client — ATAK will ask the operator to hand-place every PNG ("Select a location on the map to place: h00.png"). The wrapper is a zip containing MANIFEST/manifest.xml (MissionPackageManifest v2) with a stable uid and onReceiveImport=true, plus the payload files. Keep the uid stable across refreshes so each publish updates the same package rather than creating a new one. Keep rasters one GroundOverlay per KMZ and vectors in their own KMZ — a mixed KMZ imports as a GRG and silently drops every placemark. The full set of rules lives in What you can show in TAK clients.

The refresh loop

Because every call is idempotent, a refresh loop is stateless — regenerate, repackage, republish, no bookkeeping:
*/30 * * * *  cd /srv/myfeed && ./build.sh && ./package.sh && ./publish.sh

Changed content means a new hash and a real upload; unchanged content dedupes to a no-op. Optionally DELETE superseded hashes to keep the mission contents tidy.

Alternative: live CoT on :8089

For data shaped like events and positions rather than files, skip Marti entirely: open a TLS connection to :8089 with an enrolled client certificate and write CoT XML onto the stream. CoT's stale attribute makes stateless refresh loops trivial — re-send the current picture each run and let old markers expire on their own. Public transport and vessel-tracking APIs (Finland's Digitraffic, for instance) suit this pattern well. Mechanics are in Pushing data to TAK server.

If you want a dedicated ingest port instead of the client port, POST /Marti/api/inputs creates a new TCP/TLS CoT input at runtime — but it is not persisted to CoreConfig.xml and vanishes on pod restart. Re-POST it on every run; a 500 "Input name already exists" means all is well.

Verify, and one gotcha

GET /Marti/api/clientEndPoints lists connected clients (callsign, uid, Connected/Disconnected) — the quickest proof that your publisher identity works and your consumers are online.

And the gotcha: TAK Server takes minutes to serve Marti after a pod restart — Deployment tak-server is a single replica with Recreate strategy, so every rollout drops it, and until the JVMs are up your calls fail (and takrmapi client-zip requests 500 with TimeoutError). A refresh loop should tolerate failure and simply try again next tick.
